title: Hypermode Launch: Kevin Van Gundy

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 100%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: Hypermode is presented as a runtime and developer platform integrating models and data into AI functions with surrounding iteration and observation tools. The talk targets software builders seeking to incrementally adopt AI technologies without early architectural commitments. Covers building AI features, deploying to production, and observing inference in production. Prerequisites state no specialized skills are needed to use Hypermode for AI app development. Product launch presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair with an associated hands-on workshop. Key classification claims are directly supported by transcript excerpts graded said_in_transcript.

summary: Kevin Van Gundy launches Hypermode at the AI Engineer World's Fair, drawing on experience at a company called Cell where rapid iteration proved the winning strategy against competitors. He recounts overcoming disadvantages against JavaScript frameworks and hosting providers not through superior knowledge but by iterating quickly—trying more things faster to discover what the market wanted. He calls iteration the compound interest of software. Two key lessons emerged: developers want to incrementally adopt new technologies, and they resist committing to architectural patterns before understanding how applications will actually work. Van Gundy argues that the same fear of getting things wrong that held back web development now impedes AI adoption, and GenAI presents even more failure points—hardware, model selection, prompting, integration, monitoring, and improvement. Hypermode addresses these as a runtime integrating models and data into AI functions, surrounded by tools for rapid iteration and production observation. The platform emphasizes frictionless model switching, unified APIs for classical and AI systems, and step-by-step inference tracing. Developer experience improvements include type-ahead in existing editors without SDKs, strong defaults, and bring-your-own-stack flexibility. A notable optimization replaces traditional RAG's N+1 request pattern with a single in-memory request, saving hundreds of milliseconds per call. Hypermode also simplifies comparing inferences, tunes, and models, with dataset export for fine-tuning. Van Gundy concludes by inviting attendees to a hands-on workshop to build natural language search, intelligent sorting, outlier detection, and security features, offering $1,000 in Hypermode credits.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Background and Iteration Philosophy
sections.summary: Van Gundy recounts his experience at Cell, where rapid iteration overcame competitive disadvantages against JavaScript frameworks and hosting providers. He introduces iteration as the compound interest of software.

sections.title: Developer Needs and AI Challenges
sections.summary: Two lessons learned: developers want incremental adoption and resist early architectural commitments. Fear of getting things wrong holds back AI just as it did web. GenAI has many failure points, and teams need systems that embrace the risk of being wrong.

sections.title: Hypermode Overview
sections.summary: Hypermode is a runtime for integrating models and data into AI functions, surrounded by tools for rapid iteration and production observation. It enables incremental adoption and eventual reimagination as AI-native applications.

sections.title: Developer Experience and Features
sections.summary: Features include type-ahead in existing editors without SDKs, strong defaults, bring-your-own-stack flexibility, in-memory embedding and search replacing traditional RAG's N+1 requests, and easy comparison of inferences with dataset export for fine-tuning.

sections.title: Workshop and Closing
sections.summary: Van Gundy invites attendees to a post-lunch workshop to build natural language search, intelligent sorting, outlier detection, and security features, with a plan for production by end of next month and $1,000 in Hypermode credits.
